primary_output_claim: KOSMOS can generate scientifically useful radiobiology hypotheses, assessed here through three specific claims about DDR–p53 response, OGT/CDO1 radiation-module regulation, and a prostate-radiotherapy survival signature.
validator_anchor: Title page affiliations; Abstract and Introduction §§1–2; §3 auditing strategy
validator_rationale: The audit is authored by researchers at Henry Ford Health, Michigan State University, and Toronto Metropolitan University, outside the KOSMOS developer team. They independently reconstruct the analyses and define empirical null tests.
endpoint_anchor: Abstract; §3.1.1–3.1.3; Discussion limitations on pathway dependence and independent experimental validation
endpoint_rationale: The null-model analyses directly test statistical support for all three displayed hypotheses and expose one failure, one mixed result, and one supported association. However, they do not fully test the causal 'upstream regulator' interpretation or prospectively validate the findings in independent datasets or experiments, which the paper itself identifies as necessary.

primary_output_claim: Within the FirstProof deadline and best-of-two protocol, Aletheia autonomously solved 6 of the 10 research-level mathematics problems.
validator_anchor: Abstract; Table 1; §1 evaluation limitation; §3 expert evaluation; public raw prompts and outputs
validator_rationale: The report is written by the Aletheia team and evaluators are commissioned largely from within Google, so institutional externality is not established. Still, proof judgments are made by mathematical experts after generation, against fixed problems and disclosed outputs, with official human solutions released only after the challenge deadline.
endpoint_anchor: Table 1 expert correctness counts; §3 problem-by-problem evaluation and appendices containing the submitted proofs
endpoint_rationale: Expert assessment directly examines the correctness of each generated proof or no-output state for all ten fixed problems. This reaches the full primary claim that six problems were solved, including the disputed Problem 8 rather than validating only compilation or a component score.

primary_output_claim: Providing structured experimental hit/miss feedback enables capable LLM scientist agents to learn during iterative campaigns and materially increase discovery of gene perturbations affecting target morphological features.
validator_anchor: §3.1–3.4 experimental design; fixed JUMP-derived p-values; ten independent replicates per feature; Random Feedback control
validator_rationale: The author team constructs the campaigns and analysis, but generation cannot change the precomputed JUMP outcomes, comparison conditions are prespecified, and the decisive hit labels and exact feature-level permutation tests are separated from agent proposal generation. The random-feedback control further isolates information content from mere prompt history.
endpoint_anchor: Abstract; Table 1; §§4.1 and 4.6 random-feedback analysis; feature-level sign-flip tests in §3.4
endpoint_rationale: Cumulative unique hits directly measure discovery improvement, paired feature-level tests establish the feedback effect, and randomized hit/miss histories remove the gain. Together these tests cover the central claim that structured feedback—not static prior knowledge or history format—drives improved perturbation discovery within the stated precomputed-data setting.

primary_output_claim: AI agents can reliably perform end-to-end computational reproduction from real physics papers, correctly implementing the reported method and recovering the paper's quantitative results.
validator_anchor: Abstract and Introduction; Section 3, Benchmark Construction (domain-expert reference implementations and independent verification by a second domain expert); Section 4, Evaluation
validator_rationale: The benchmark authors commissioned the references, so institutional externality is not established; however, evaluated agents cannot adapt to the verified ground truth, and a second domain expert independently checks each task's method, implementation, and physical behavior.
endpoint_anchor: Abstract and Introduction; Section 3, Benchmark Construction; Section 4, Evaluation (methodology understanding, code correctness, data reproduction accuracy, and task completion)
endpoint_rationale: The reference implementation and verified numerical ground truth directly test the claimed end-to-end reproduction, while method agreement, code correctness, reproduced quantities, and physical plausibility cover its central failure conditions.

primary_output_claim: VERITAS can autonomously carry out end-to-end hypothesis testing on medical-imaging data and produce statistically correct, power-aware, auditable Supported, Refuted, Underpowered, or Invalid conclusions.
validator_anchor: Introduction and Contributions; Section 3.4, Benchmark & Evaluation (canonical reference statistics computed from ground-truth masks and metadata, validated by a domain expert)
validator_rationale: The decisive reference statistics and their expert validation are described, but the paper does not document an external institution, blinded or held-out evaluator, independent reproduction, or another adequate separation from the author team.
endpoint_anchor: Introduction and Contributions; Sections 3.3-3.4, Evidence Label Framework and Benchmark & Evaluation
endpoint_rationale: Canonical dataset-derived statistics are compared directly with the system's verdicts and mechanically derived evidence labels; positive, negative/no-effect, underpowered, and untestable controls test the conclusion and its central statistical failure conditions.

primary_output_claim: AI agents can conduct long-horizon analysis of raw or near-raw spatial-biology data and experimental context, without a prescribed method, to recover correct complex scientific conclusions.
validator_anchor: Abstract; Figure 2 and Benchmark Design (independent reanalysis, randomized expert review, trajectory inspection, anonymized data, and controlled answer surfaces)
validator_rationale: Institutional externality is not documented, but candidate claims are independently reproduced and randomly peer-reviewed before evaluation, and agents receive anonymized data while decisive answers are fixed behind controlled grading procedures.
endpoint_anchor: Abstract; Introduction; Benchmark Design; Endpoint grading (deterministic grading of the final structured scientific answer)
endpoint_rationale: The scored endpoint is the target biological conclusion itself, not merely workflow execution; reproduction and review reject unstable claims, and the deterministic final-answer grader directly tests whether the agent recovered the curated conclusion, with trajectory rubrics used only diagnostically.

primary_output_claim: HLER's human-gated, deterministic decision architecture materially reduces and contains unreliable AI-assisted empirical-social-science outputs relative to an otherwise matched unconstrained multi-agent workflow.
validator_rationale: The author team commissions the reference assessment, so institutional externality is not established; however, the same three PhD-level experts independently grade all 280 runs while blinded to pipeline configuration under a pre-specified rubric and majority rule, separating decisive grading from generation and treatment identity.
endpoint_rationale: The rubric directly tests necessary scientific dimensions—feasibility, identification credibility, and consistency—and detects whether critical defects escape containment, so it meaningfully supports the architecture's reliability claim. It does not reproduce the empirical findings or exhaust their substantive validity; the authors explicitly state that these metrics are necessary but not sufficient for replicable findings and that HLER does not guarantee valid identification.

primary_output_claim: Intervention-centered Auto Research produces frozen feature, model, representation, and data decisions whose advantages transfer beyond adaptive feedback, yielding reusable intervention evidence and an information-dependent hierarchy for materials-property prediction.
validator_anchor: §3 Frozen-Code Held-Out Transfer and Outer-holdout protocol; Fig. 1; §4 Experimental Design
validator_rationale: The decisive reference outcomes are official Matbench fold-0 materials-property labels originating outside both the agent developers and evaluating author team. Agent processes never receive those labels; frozen code and choices are evaluated once against the externally produced holdout through a trusted evaluator.
endpoint_anchor: Abstract; Introduction contributions; Fig. 2; Results 'Outer Evidence Confirms Nine, Rejects One' and 'Intervention Hierarchies Depend on Input'; §6 Conclusion
endpoint_rationale: The untouched outer labels directly test predictive transfer, selection regret, alternative ordering, and the compatibility of frozen interventions, including rejection of one inner-endorsed choice. They do not independently validate the broader explanatory interpretation that the observed axis hierarchy identifies reusable materials-science mechanisms or the general allocation principle beyond these ten benchmark endpoints; this is predictive transfer without complete validation of the claimed explanation.
